issue.title: Persist the solve queue and recovery state (link-cli + Links Notation triple storage on a host volume, Telegram as fallback) so a root container restart continues the queue

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, 193 GB disk, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store (`overlayfs` snapshotter), live-restore disabled. Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot`; tasks run as `$ --isolated docker` containers from `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`. hive-mind 2.34.0, start-command 0.35.4.

At 12:11:39 UTC the kernel OOM-killed the **host dockerd** (7.3 GB RSS, caused by ~22 concurrent `docker diff` calls from a disk-cleanup tool test suite run inside the root container — link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22). systemd restarted dockerd, which SIGKILLed every running container (exit 137): the root `hive-mind` container and four `/codex` solve tasks for link-assistant/router#724, #725, #727, #728. The root container was started again manually at 13:31 UTC; the bot then ran its built-in kill recovery.

## Problem

The solve queue exists only in the bot's memory. When the root container died, **32 queued tasks were lost** (27 codex, 5 claude). After the restart `/queue` showed `Completed: 0, Failed: 0` and `/limits` showed every queue at `pending: 0`.

Last `/limits` before the crash (bot log):
```
claude (pending: 5, processing: 1)
codex (pending: 27, processing: 4)
```

The only reason the list below is known is that the old container log still had the `Enqueued:`/`Starting:` lines and the `/codex raw text: …` lines, from which an external script (`auto-recovery.mjs` in our control repository) replayed the queue:

<details><summary>Lost items (id, tool, url)</summary>

```

```
</details>

Other state needed for recovery also lives in the container's writable layer only: `~/.hive-mind/state/sessions.json` (tracked sessions), start-command's execution store and logs under `/tmp/start-command`. A redeploy (`docker rm` + `docker run`) or a lost container loses all of it.

## Requirements

1. Persist the queue (every item with its full command, args, requester, chat/message ids, tool, status, timestamps) and all other state the bot needs to continue after a restart: tracked sessions, recovery attempts, throttling/start-interval state, message ids it keeps editing.
2. Use the associative stack as described in https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/main/docs/associative-tech-stack.md — **triple storage**, each able to rebuild the others:
   - a binary links store (doublets via the `link-cli` library / its transactional, fsynced store),
   - a text Links Notation (`.lino`) projection, written atomically, human-readable and diffable,
   - a `link-cli` database for querying.
3. Keep it in a small database in the hive-mind application folder on a **volume mounted from the host** (for example `/root/.hive-mind/state` → `/home/box/.hive-mind/state`), so it survives `docker rm`, a dockerd crash and a redeploy. Document the mount in the Docker docs and deploy examples.
4. On startup, load the stored queue and continue it automatically: re-enqueue pending items in their original order, reconcile items that were `starting`/`processing` against `$ --list` and running containers, and tell the chat what was restored.
5. If both link stores are missing or corrupted, fall back to the **Telegram messages as the source of truth**: rebuild the queue from the bot's own queue/status messages and the original commands (the bot already knows the message ids it edits), and as a last resort from the bot log (`Enqueued:` / `Starting:` / `raw text:` lines).
6. Tests: kill the bot process and the container with items queued, processing and in recovery, then check that everything continues without manual action.

## Related

- `sessions.json` / `sessions-events.jsonl` ([session-store.lib.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/session-store.lib.mjs#L130-L135)) already persist tracked sessions, but in the container layer and not the queue (`SolveQueue` keeps `queues`, `processing`, `completed`, `failed` in memory: [telegram-solve-queue.lib.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/790c18dec9ec0dd2281de05a48f2047690a60415/src/telegram-solve-queue.lib.mjs#L159-L180)).

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

Related: #2887, #2888, #2889 (kill recovery after the same incident).

issue.title: fix(isolation): resume killed docker sessions with docker start and a command handoff; guard and clean up snapshots (#2889)

labels.name: formal-ai-draft
labels.description: Pull request drafted by the Formal AI draft workflow

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
Fixes #2889.

In-place kill recovery always passed the recovery command to `$ --resume <uuid> -- <command>`. start-command handles that by `docker commit`ting the container's **whole writable layer** to an image (`docker-snapshot` mode). After the dockerd restart on 2026-10-09, four recoveries (11 / 21.2 / 23.5 / 36.8 GiB layers) committed at the same time on the containerd image store. They used ~280 % CPU for 30+ minutes, took free disk from 52 GB to 2 GB, and two failed with `no space left on device`. The two that succeeded left their originals and images behind.

Case study (data, timeline, requirements R1–R10, root causes, alternatives, research): [`docs/case-studies/issue-2889/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2889-b3cf2ad55a40/docs/case-studies/issue-2889/README.md)

## What changes

### Resume in place with `docker start` and a command handoff (no copy)

Every task container is now created with a short prefix in front of its gated command (`src/docker-resume-handoff.lib.mjs`):

```sh
h='/tmp/hive-mind-resume-command-<session id>'; if [ -f "$h" ]; then exec sh "$h"; fi; <gate loop>; exec <task>
```

To recover a killed session the bot:

1. reads the handoff path back from the container's `Config.Cmd`, so legacy containers are recognised;
2. writes `exec <recovery command>` there with `docker cp`, which works on a stopped container;
3. runs `$ --resume <uuid>` **without** a command.

start-command then picks `docker-start` and restarts the **same** container. It keeps the same ID, writable layer (repo, build cache) and HostConfig (CPU/RAM limits). Nothing is committed.

### Guarded snapshot for containers created before this change

`src/docker-resume-snapshot-guard.lib.mjs`, used by `resumeWithSnapshot` in `src/session-kill-resume.in-place.lib.mjs`:

- **one snapshot at a time** (in-process queue);
- **disk headroom preflight**: free space on the Docker data root ≥ 2 × the writable layer (compressed blob + unpacked snapshot on containerd) + 10 GiB. Otherwise the recovery waits, re-checking every 30 s for up to 10 min, then falls back to a fresh launch rather than fill the disk. Unknown sizes fail open (the old behaviour);
- the derived container gets the handoff prefix as well, so its next recovery is a `docker start`;
- the **stopped original is removed** with `docker rm` (never `-f`) once the derived container runs, unless `HIVE_MIND_KEEP_TASK_CONTAINER=always`.

### Cleanup when the task finishes

The `start-command-resume/*` images a session's recoveries created are tracked per session (`containerSnapshotImages`, persisted in the session store) and carried from the killed session to its recovery. They are removed with `docker rmi` together with the finished task's container. Kept containers list them with the `docker rmi` command. A container restarted with `docker start` is never `docker rm -f`'d by the killed session's completion.

### Telegram status

`reportRecoveryLifecycle` takes a `detail` line, and a changed detail updates the message within the same phase. Examples:

- "Restarting the same container with docker start (no filesystem copy)."
- "Waiting for disk: …"
- "Waiting for 1 other container snapshot to finish first."
- "Snapshotting the 23.5 GiB container filesystem …"

### Applied everywhere

A `docker start` recovery keeps the container but changes the tracking key. Every Docker probe now uses `getDockerTaskContainerName` instead of the key: the resource monitor, the OOM probe, the stale-executing probe and completion removal.

### Debug output

`[VERBOSE] docker-resume-handoff:` and `[VERBOSE] In-place resume of …` lines are printed on every decision: handoff found or not, disk measurements, queue position, and removal results.

## Upstream

- link-foundation/start#193 (concurrent `$ --resume` loses the execution record): fixed in start#196, as noted on the issue. With 0.36.0, a concurrent second resume of the same execution is now rejected by the launch reservation.
- **Filed link-foundation/start#198**: `--resume <id> -- <command>` copies the whole writable layer with no disk preflight, no serialization and no cleanup. It includes a bounded reproduction on 0.36.0, the handoff workaround, and fix suggestions (a copy-free in-place command resume, a preflight, a lock, a `--remove-original` option, and image cleanup).

## Reproduction and tests

| What | How |
| --- | --- |
| Unit / integration (default suite, 72 assertions) | `node tests/test-issue-2889-docker-resume-handoff.mjs`. It covers: the handoff prefix run in a real `sh`; Docker helpers on errors; the disk guard and queue; the docker-start path (tracking keys, handoff write failure, relaunch race); the snapshot path (original removal, `always`, waiting for disk, serialization); the completion action after a recovery; and the lifecycle detail line. Each fix was reverted in turn to confirm that the tests fail without it. |
| Updated | `tests/test-issue-2189-same-container-resume.mjs` (handoff-wrapped recovery command) |
| Real Docker, the fix | `node experiments/issue-2889-docker-start-handoff.mjs --compare-snapshot` launches like Hive Mind, kills, hands off and resumes. Result: `docker-start`, same container ID, the task's files present, no image or `-resume-` container. The old path on a 64 MiB layer made a 74.9 MB image ([log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2889-b3cf2ad55a40/docs/case-studies/issue-2889/data/docker-start-handoff-experiment.log)). |
| Real Docker, the upstream problem | `experiments/issue-2889-concurrent-snapshot-resume.sh` on start-command 0.36.0: two concurrent commits, no disk check, originals and images left behind ([log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2889-b3cf2ad55a40/docs/case-studies/issue-2889/data/concurrent-snapshot-resume-start-0.36.0.log)) |
| Manual recovery | `examples/issue-2889-manual-docker-start-recovery.sh <container> <command...>` (verified on start-command 0.35.4 and 0.36.0) |

## Limitations

- Containers created **before** this change still need one snapshot for their first recovery. It is now bounded (serialized, headroom, original removed), but it is still a full copy. The derived container has the handoff, so later recoveries are copy-free.
- Dropping regenerable caches (`target/`, `node_modules/.cache`) before a snapshot is not done. The container is stopped, starting it re-runs its old command, and editing snapshotter directories needs host root. The copy-free path makes it unnecessary for new containers.
- The headroom check measures the Docker data root (`DockerRootDir`). A separate containerd root on another filesystem is not measured (in the incident both were on `/`).
- The snapshot queue is per bot process.

## Also in this PR

- **Bun 1.4.2 → 1.4.3** in `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.dind` and `coolify/Dockerfile`. Bun 1.4.3 was released on 2026-10-10, and the dependency-freshness gate failed this PR's CI with "3 stale" ([run 38028420250](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/38028420250)). The issue #2187 pin tests now require the current Bun release, as they already do for Node.js, instead of the Box base's 1.4.2.

issue.title: Recommend and preflight-check Docker "live-restore": true so a dockerd restart no longer kills the bot and every task

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Incident context (2026-10-09)

Host: Ubuntu 24.04, 6 CPU, 11.7 GB RAM, Docker 29.6.1 (containerd image store), **no `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, so `live-restore` was off** (`docker info -f '{{.LiveRestoreEnabled}}'` → `false`). Root container `hive-mind` (DinD variant, `--restart unless-stopped`) runs `hive-telegram-bot` and launches tasks on the host daemon as `$ --isolated docker` containers. hive-mind 2.34.0.

At 12:11:39 UTC the kernel OOM-killed the **host dockerd**. systemd restarted it within seconds, and on restore dockerd force-killed every container (exit 137): the root container and all four running `/codex` tasks (link-assistant/router #724, #725, #727, #728). The in-memory solve queue (32 items) was lost (#2890), and kill recovery then hit #2887, #2888, #2889 and #2892.

```
14:11:39 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 823 (dockerd) … anon-rss:7302520kB
14:11:41 systemd: docker.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
14:11:45 dockerd: Loading containers: start.
14:11:55 dockerd: Container failed to exit within 10s of signal 15 - using the force container=…
```

## Problem

With the Docker default (`live-restore: false`), **any** dockerd restart kills every container: crash, OOM kill, `apt upgrade docker-ce`, `systemctl restart docker`. For hive-mind that is the worst possible failure. One daemon hiccup takes down the bot, every running task and the queue together, and then everything has to be recovered from snapshots.

Container processes do not depend on dockerd. They are children of `containerd-shim`. With [`"live-restore": true`](https://docs.docker.com/engine/daemon/live-restore/) dockerd re-attaches to them after a restart, and the bot and tasks keep running. That one setting would have prevented this whole incident.

Nothing in hive-mind mentions this today (no `live-restore` / `daemon.json` in `docs/` or `src/`), and the startup preflight (`preflightDockerIsolation` in `src/isolation-runner.lib.mjs`) already checks the storage driver and disk space but not this.

## Working example (applied on the incident host)

The setting can be turned on **without restarting dockerd**, because `live-restore` is a reloadable option (SIGHUP via `systemctl reload docker`). Restarting the daemon to apply it would itself kill every container. Verified on the live host with tasks running and a `docker commit` in progress. No container was affected:

```bash
python3 -c 'import json,os
p="/etc/docker/daemon.json"
d=json.load(open(p)) if os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p) else {}
changed=d.get("live-restore") is not True
d["live-restore"]=True
os.makedirs("/etc/docker",exist_ok=True)
changed and open(p,"w").write(json.dumps(d,indent=2)+"\n")
print("changed" if changed else "unchanged")'
systemctl reload docker        # NOT restart
docker info -f '{{.LiveRestoreEnabled}}'   # → true
```
```
dockerd: Got signal to reload configuration config-file=/etc/docker/daemon.json
dockerd: Reloaded configuration config="{… \"live-restore\":true, …}"
```

Our deploy script now does this on every deploy. It merges the key into an existing `daemon.json` and keeps the other keys, leaves invalid JSON alone with a warning, reloads, and verifies `LiveRestoreEnabled`.

## Suggested fix

1. **Startup preflight warning:** in `preflightDockerIsolation` (and/or at bot start when `--isolation docker`), read `docker info -f '{{.LiveRestoreEnabled}}'` from the daemon the bot launches tasks on. If it is `false`, warn loudly with the exact remediation above, including "use `systemctl reload docker`, never `restart`, while containers are running". This is diagnostic only and never blocks startup, like the existing storage-driver and disk checks. Add tests with an injectable probe, like `checkStorageDriver`.
2. **Docs:** add a "Host Docker daemon settings" section to `docs/DOCKER.md` (and the `zh`/`hi`/`ru` translations), referenced from the Quick Start / Option 3 instructions and the README install section. It should cover `live-restore: true`, why it matters for hive-mind (bot + all tasks + in-memory queue die together on a daemon restart), how to apply it without a restart, and its limits (it does not survive a host reboot; containers still need `--restart unless-stopped` and queue persistence from #2890).
3. **Any hive-mind install/deploy scripts** that install Docker on a host should write the setting the same way, merging rather than overwriting `daemon.json`.
4. **Optional, nested daemon:** the DinD entrypoint in link-foundation/box starts the inner dockerd with `nohup` and nothing restarts it, so `--live-restore` there only helps when the inner daemon is restarted by hand. It is low priority, but passing `--live-restore` would be harmless and consistent.

Related: #2892 (daemon-restart kills reported as OOM), #2890 (queue persistence), #2889 (snapshot recovery cost, which live-restore avoids entirely for daemon restarts), link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22 (the trigger of the dockerd OOM).

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

issue.title: $ --resume starts the new container, then fails to save the record (lock timeout), leaving it running untracked

repository.name: start
repository.description: Gamification of coding, execute any command with ability to auto-report issues on GitHub

issue.body:
## Problem

`$ --resume <uuid> -- <command>` (docker-snapshot mode, start-command 0.35.4) **started the new container and then failed to save the execution record**. The container keeps running, but start-command no longer knows about it:

```
$ --resume deb9c2e9-8234-43ef-9648-e102f5d34ebd --output-format json -- solve https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/728 … --resume 01a1200a-…
error: Failed to acquire lock for database write
      at save (start-command/src/lib/execution-store.js:536:17)
      at resumeExecution (start-command/src/lib/execution-resume.js:493:9)
      at handleResumeQuery (start-command/src/lib/query-commands.js:60:11)
```

Afterwards:
- `docker ps`: `eec34a2b-…-resume-1-resume-2  Up 22 minutes` (the task is working fine).
- `$ --list`: the execution still says `"sessionName": "eec34a2b-…-resume-1", "status": "executed", "exitCode": 127, "resumeCount": 1`, the previous failed attempt.
- No completion watcher was attached, so the container's exit will never be written to the execution log, and `$ --status` / `--list` report the old attempt.

It happened to two of two resumes started at the same time (router#724 and router#728) while other `$` processes (another `$ --resume` blocked in a 10-minute `docker commit`, and the hive-mind bot polling `$ --list`/`--status`) were using the store.

Consequence: anything that relies on the record to decide whether a task is running treats it as dead. An automatic recovery script re-resumed both running tasks and had to be stopped before it launched duplicate solvers.

## Root cause

- [`resumeExecution`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/d7e83641815cc7e8e26757f77a6f61f22924c1a7/js/src/lib/execution-resume.js#L468-L494) runs the plan's steps (`docker commit`, `docker run`) first and only then calls `store.save(updated)` (L493). A save failure throws after the container is already running.
- [`LockManager.acquire`](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/d7e83641815cc7e8e26757f77a6f61f22924c1a7/js/src/lib/execution-store.js#L227) gives up after `LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000` ([L54](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/d7e83641815cc7e8e26757f77a6f61f22924c1a7/js/src/lib/execution-store.js#L54)). A store lock can be held for that long while another process is busy.

## Suggested fix

1. Write the "attempt N launching, session `<new name>`" record **before** `docker run` and only finalize it afterwards, so a crash or lock failure still leaves the record pointing at the new container.
2. Retry the save with backoff (well beyond 30 s) after a launch. If it still fails, stop/remove the just-started container, or print a machine-readable error naming it so the caller can recover. Today the error hides that the launch succeeded.
3. Never hold the store lock during long operations (`docker commit`/`run`). Check every writer for that.
4. `$ --status` / `--list` could reconcile `<sessionName>-resume-*` containers that exist in Docker but not in the record.

## Workaround

Detect running containers by name family (`<original>` / `<original>-resume-…`) instead of trusting the record.

---

issue.title: /limits shows processing: 0 for running docker-isolated tasks (pgrep sees only the bot container, tracked count is in-memory only), and dispatch throttling uses the same wrong count

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
## Problem

`/limits` shows `codex (pending: 0, processing: 0)` while **four** `/codex` tasks are running (`--isolation docker`, link-assistant/router #724, #725, #727, #728). Each one has a live `codex exec resume <thread>` process writing to its rollout every few seconds.

```
Queues
claude (pending: 0, processing: 0)
agent (pending: 0, processing: 0)
codex (pending: 0, processing: 0)      ← 4 codex tasks running
qwen (pending: 0, processing: 0)
gemini (pending: 0, processing: 0)
```

Context: the 2026-10-09 incident (#2892, #2887, #2889, #2900). The host dockerd was OOM-killed and its restart killed the root container and all tasks. The bot's kill recovery failed (#2887), and the four tasks were then resumed by an operator recovery script (`$ --resume <uuid>`, docker-snapshot mode). That script was written because the built-in recovery failed.

## Root causes

The count is computed by `getExternalProcessingSnapshot()` in `src/telegram-solve-queue.lib.mjs` as `max(pgrep count, tracked isolated sessions)`. Both sources miss docker-isolated tasks the bot is not tracking in memory:

1. **`pgrep -x codex` runs in the bot container's PID namespace** (`getRunningProcesses()` in `telegram-solve-queue.helpers.lib.mjs`). With `--isolation docker`, every AI CLI process runs in a sibling container, so this source is **always 0** for docker isolation.
2. **The tracked-session count only covers the in-memory `activeSessions` map** (`getRunningTrackedIsolationSessions()` in `session-monitor.queries.lib.mjs`). That map is filled only by tasks the bot launched itself and, once, at startup from `~/.hive-mind/state/sessions.json` (`resumeTrackedSessions()` in `bot-lifecycle.lib.mjs`). Here the bot had already emitted `session_completed … "status":"oom-killed"` / `"failed"` for all four sessions during its failed recovery, so `sessions.json` has **0 entries**. Tasks resumed outside the bot are never adopted.
3. **Even for tracked sessions, liveness comes from `$ --status`**, which reports these running tasks as `executed 137/127`. start-command could not save any record since 14:32 UTC because of a dead 0-byte `executions.lock` (root cause in link-foundation/start#193).

## Why it matters beyond the display

The same snapshot drives dispatch. `canStartCommand()` uses `totalProcessing = this.processing.size + externalProcessing.total` for `checkSystemResources()`, and `hasRunningToolProcess`/`toolProcessingCount` for `checkApiLimits()` and one-at-a-time per tool. With four codex tasks invisible, the bot will start new codex tasks as if none were running. On this host (11.7 GB RAM, each task using 2.3–2.5 GiB of its 2.92 GiB limit) that is exactly the overcommit that leads to OOM kills.

## Suggested fix

1. **Count from ground truth, not memory.** For `--isolation docker`, list running task containers on the daemon the bot launches into. Add labels at launch, e.g. `--label hive-mind.tool=codex --label hive-mind.url=<issue/pr url> --label start-command.uuid=<uuid>`. Today task containers carry only the image labels, so they cannot be attributed. Re-apply the labels on every `$ --resume` `docker run`, because `docker commit` does not carry container labels to the new container. Then `processing[tool] = count(docker ps --filter label=hive-mind.tool=<tool>)`. For older unlabeled containers, fall back to `$ --list` records whose `options.sessionName` (or `sessionNameHistory`) family matches a running container name.
2. **Adopt orphans.** When a labelled (or `$ --list`-matched) running task container is not in `activeSessions`, re-track it with url/tool/uuid from its labels or record. The bot then monitors it, sends the completion notice, and keeps `sessions.json` correct. Do this periodically, not only at startup. Together with #2890 (durable queue/state), a root-container restart then continues monitoring everything that is actually running.
3. **Use `pgrep` only for `--isolation none`.** For docker isolation, if a per-process count is wanted, use `docker top <container>` on the attributed containers.
4. **Show the source in `/limits`** (e.g. `codex (pending: 0, processing: 4, 2 untracked)`), so an untracked or orphaned task is visible instead of silently counted as 0.
5. Tests: a running labelled container that is not in `activeSessions` must be counted, adopted, and must block one-at-a-time dispatch for its tool. `$ --status` reporting `executed` for a container that `docker ps` shows as running must be counted as running.

Related: #2887, #2889, #2890, #2892, #2900, link-foundation/start#193.

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

body:
The start-command tracking failure referenced by this incident is fixed in [start PR #196](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/pull/196), in both JavaScript and Rust. The separate writable-layer/snapshot storage policy remains a Hive Mind concern.

The directly observed blocker was an empty `executions.lock`. The old writer published the shared lock before populating its owner JSON; disk-full failure or a crash could leave a malformed lock that never became reclaimable. The resume flow also launched the replacement before saving its identity, and a JS save exception skipped completion-watcher attachment. A partial in-place database write could destroy even an earlier reservation. The supplied incident does not establish that a database lock was held throughout `docker commit`.

Reproduction and regression coverage in the PR checkout:

```sh
bun test ./js/test/regression-193.js
cd rust && cargo test --test regression_193
cargo test partial_disk_full_write_preserves_reservation_and_removes_temporary_file
```

These bounded tests inject empty/truncated old locks, partial ENOSPC-equivalent writes, reservation failures and save failures after an accepted launch. They assert exact attempt/session persistence before Docker side effects, concurrent store writes during a Docker hook, watcher attachment, confirmed stop, and machine-readable identity if stopping fails. They do not fill the host disk.

For existing installations, pause concurrent recovery, inspect replacement containers by exact/name-family identity, and remove a malformed abandoned lock only after verifying that no writer owns it. Serialize unavoidable snapshots, preflight writable-layer size/free space, and discard regenerable build caches where appropriate. These reduce disk pressure but do not fix tracking.

The code fix reserves the launch durably, releases the database lock before Docker work, publishes populated locks atomically, atomically replaces the database, and attaches the watcher even if the final save fails. A failed final save triggers a stop attempt and `LAUNCH_PERSISTENCE_FAILED` JSON containing UUID, exact container name and `running`; a stop failure leaves the durable reservation available for reconciliation.

[Complete case study, UTC timeline, full redacted archives and SHA-256 manifests](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/tree/issue-195-cd307f03a9cf/docs/case-studies/issue-193). The storage-side code solution suggested here remains an in-place command handoff before start, with serialization/headroom checks for snapshots that cannot be avoided.

issue.title: feat: Docker resource controls and reliable execution recovery

repository.name: start
repository.description: Gamification of coding, execute any command with ability to auto-report issues on GitHub

issue.body:
Docker tasks can now receive launch and recovery resource limits, opt into delayed CPU penalties, and report memory diagnostics through remote/DinD daemons. Launch identities are saved before Docker side effects, and terminal OOM classification requires exit-time evidence rather than historical child-process kills.

This single PR implements all six issues in both JavaScript and Rust:

| Issue | Result |
| --- | --- |
| #189 | Opt-in CPU penalty with all requested flags/defaults, timestamp-weighted full windows, outage/restart resets, daemon resize handling, finite base restoration, transition logs and status. Works with attached/detached execution and disabled tracking. |
| #190 | `--memory`, `--memory-swap` and `--cpus` accept absolute values, daemon percentages and uniform random ranges. Resolve before run/create, default swap to memory, record requested/resolved values, preserve choices on plain resume and forward raw settings through JS isolation stacks. |
| #191 | `--on-kill-resume-memory` and manual resume overrides update limits before starting the command; snapshot replacements receive limits at creation. Fresh qualifying OOM recoveries draw again and log/store old/new/spec values. Ordinary exit 0/1 remains final. |
| #192 | Container-attributed local cgroups first, daemon exec fallback in private namespaces, last-good samples across outages, and an unconditional `Memory:` line with the observed unavailability reason and HostConfig limit. Missing shells do not abort execution. |
| #193 | Durable launch reservations on initial/manual/automatic paths, populated atomic lock publication, short malformed-lock grace, atomic database replacement, and no database lock across Docker work. Postlaunch save failure still attaches the watcher, attempts to stop the container and returns machine-readable identity/running state. |
| #194 | Historical `OOMKilled`/counters plus 137 now yield unknown SIGKILL. A fresh sampled delta can establish terminal OOM; Docker service journal evidence plus the exact container's force-kill line establishes daemon restart and takes precedence. Evidence survives log loss and is shared by attached diagnostics, finalization, status/list and recovery. |

The [complete numbered requirement/solution checklist](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-195-cd307f03a9cf/docs/case-studies/issue-195/requirements.md) covers every issue and comment requirement. [Research and alternatives](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-195-cd307f03a9cf/docs/case-studies/issue-195/research.md) evaluate Docker/cgroup semantics, Hive Mind's CPU policy, dockerode, Bollard, proper-lockfile and fs2. The implementation reuses the existing Docker CLI and shared file format without new dependencies. Existing legacy CPU period/quota configurations remain compatible with in-place updates.

[Tracking case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/tree/issue-195-cd307f03a9cf/docs/case-studies/issue-193) and [exit-attribution case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/tree/issue-195-cd307f03a9cf/docs/case-studies/issue-194) include UTC timelines, evidence versus inference, all original reports/comments, complete redacted incident archives and SHA-256 manifests. Debug tracing remains off by default. Downstream reports include reproduction, workarounds and code-fix recommendations.

Validation:

- Final-head CI on `e9cbeb4`: JavaScript, Rust, Security, Workflows and Broken Link Checker all pass. Linux/macOS/Windows platform tests and both coverage gates pass.
- JavaScript: `bun run check`; full suite with coverage, 1,112 passing tests; 89.92% line coverage exceeds the existing 45% gate.
- Rust: `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --all-targets --all-features` (986 passing tests); six documentation tests.
- Test parity, all five documented examples, shared-script syntax and evidence integrity/credential scans pass. Offline CI regressions verify cached tags, mirror fallback, bounded failure, and no Alpine probes against unavailable or Windows-mode daemons.
- New regression files #189–194 in each implementation reproduce the defects and test both ordinary and failure paths. Finite shell fixtures verify CPU apply/lift/reapply with tracking disabled, remote memory sampling, missing shells, shared namespaces and outages. Lock/store tests inject malformed owner data, partial ENOSPC writes, concurrent writers, reservation failure and postlaunch persistence failure.
- Real Docker smoke tests pass for ordinary attached and detached execution in both CLIs, including final exit/status and the unconditional memory diagnostic.

Reproduction commands:

```sh
bun test ./js/test/regression-189.js ./js/test/regression-190.js ./js/test/regression-191.js ./js/test/regression-192.js ./js/test/regression-193.js ./js/test/regression-194.js
cd rust
cargo test --test regression_189 --test regression_190 --test regression_191 --test regression_192 --test regression_193 --test regression_194
```

All six issues are implemented; none is deferred or treated as already resolved. Actual CPU/memory enforcement and main-process cgroup OOM could not be reproduced on this runner: runc rejects resource-limited containers because its cgroup is in threaded mode. The bounded real-resource probe and its complete failure output are committed. No host-wide OOM, disk-fill or live daemon restart was induced; those supplied incidents are reproduced with bounded fault/journal fixtures. The sampled-delta option allowed by #194 provides temporal evidence, not exact main-PID proof; inaccessible journals or missing final samples yield unknown cause. See [verification and reproduction limits](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-195-cd307f03a9cf/docs/case-studies/issue-195/verification.md).

[CI investigation](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/blob/issue-195-cd307f03a9cf/docs/case-studies/issue-195/ci-investigation.md) records preserved failed-run logs and the fixes: official image preloading with bounded mirror fallback, checksum-verified native Actionlint, valid Rust action pins, Windows test portability, and correct Linux-container capability checks for the existing shell tests. Real Docker integration tests and existing quality gates remain enabled.

Includes a JavaScript minor changeset and Rust minor changelog fragment; release versions remain managed by CI.

Downstream reports: [tracking failure and storage recommendations](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2889#issuecomment-6089357064), [exit attribution and daemon workarounds](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2892#issuecomment-6089357423).

issue.title: JavaScript-first Router with full Rust parity via meta-language translation; bulk sub-agent drafting with one CI/CD push gate; Rust CI/CD starts only after JavaScript CI/CD passes
issue.body:
## Goal

Make Router development fast and light on the machines that run it:

1. **JavaScript first.** Every feature is implemented and tested in JavaScript first, and the Rust code is produced from it by automated translation through [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language).
2. **Router gets a native JavaScript implementation with full feature parity** with the Rust one, enforced in CI like meta-language's parity gate. Today `packages/javascript` (`@link-assistant/router`) is a wrapper that runs the Rust binary (`ROUTER_BIN`), not an implementation.
3. **Bulk changes with sub-agents, and one push gate.** Several sub-agents draft all requirements in bulk. Exactly **one** sub-agent owns `git push`: it watches CI/CD, drafts the fixes for **all** failures of the last run, and pushes only once they are all drafted.
4. **Rust CI/CD cannot start until JavaScript CI/CD has fully passed.**

**Scope: this is the rule for all big Rust projects, not only Router.** Wherever a project has a lot of Rust code, development is JavaScript first, with a native JavaScript implementation at full parity, Rust produced by meta-language translation, a single CI/CD push gate, and Rust CI/CD gated on green JavaScript CI/CD. Router is where it is set up and proven first. Requirement 8 carries it to the other repositories.

## Evidence 1: latest unfinished pull requests with a lot of Rust

CI runs counted with `gh run list --branch <head>` on 2026-10-10.

| PR | Size | Commits | CI on the branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| link-foundation/meta-language#201 (draft) | +134,131 / −5,667 | 58 | `CI`: **44 runs, 0 green**, 25 failed, **19 cancelled** |
| link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#184 (draft) | +400,307 / −9,680 | 100+ | `issue-183-acceptance` **0/15 green**; `formal-corpus` 5 failed, `tests` 4 failed |
| link-assistant/formal-ai#1188 | +1,410,501 / −200,572 | 100+ | `CI/CD Pipeline` **0/11 green**, `Layered CI` **0/12**, `Coverage` 0/11 (5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 7 failed |
| link-assistant/router#749 (draft, for #724) | +15,086 / −388 | 33 | `CI/CD Pipeline` **3/18 green**, 9 failed, **5 cancelled** |

Pattern: many small pushes, each one starting the whole matrix and cancelling the previous run. Most runs are red or cancelled, so a full green run is rare even after dozens of pushes. The same workflows are re-run for every push while fixes arrive one at a time.

What already works and should be reused:

- **meta-language**: Rust and JavaScript side by side with a data-driven parity gate (`parity/language-features.json` + `js/scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`), run by both `rust.yml` and `js.yml`, so changing one language without the other fails CI. Translation capabilities and boundaries are documented in `docs/four-language-contracts.md` and `docs/translation-rules.md`.
- **relative-meta-logic**: a dedicated `parity` workflow (15/15 green on #184) next to the Rust/JS jobs.
- **formal-ai**: "JS server parity" in #1188, and the associative stack in `docs/associative-tech-stack.md`.

## Evidence 2: what Rust builds cost on the agent host (2026-10-09 incident)

Router tasks (#724, #725, #727, #728), each in a hive-mind task container with a 2.92 GiB memory limit on an 11.7 GB / 6 CPU host:

- `rustc`/`clippy-driver` were OOM-killed inside the containers again and again: #724 ×5, #725 ×3, #727 ×2, #728 ×2 (kernel `Memory cgroup out of memory`). The agents had to write their own workarounds (`experiments/issue-719/bounded-build.py`, `ROUTER_BUILD_RSS_LIMIT_MIB=2450`, `target/local-unit-shards`, a copied `target/debug-initial`).
- `target/` per task: **17–30 GiB** (#724: 21.2 GiB old + 11.5 GiB resumed work dir; #727: 17.2 GiB; #728: 8.6 + 2.2 GiB). One task's writable layer reached 35.7 GiB, almost all of it `target/` and `~/.cargo/registry`. `target/semver-checks` alone was 1 GiB.
- A Rust build kept one task at about 110–135% CPU for hours; #724 (PR #749) has been running for 8+ hours.
- Disk use from these builds made recovery snapshots 46–63 GB per task and contributed to the disk filling up (link-assistant/hive-mind#2889).

Nearly all of that load is local Rust compilation. JavaScript tests need no compile step and a fraction of the memory and disk.

## Requirements

1. **Case study.** Collect the experience of the PRs above, and of the other Rust-heavy repositories (link-foundation/link-cli, link-foundation/links-notation, link-foundation/start, link-assistant/calculator), in `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}`: what made CI green, what caused repeated red/cancelled runs, how parity is enforced, and what translation through meta-language supports today. Turn the results into the rules below.
2. **Native JavaScript Router with full parity.** Implement Router's logic natively in JavaScript (Node 20+ and Bun), not as a wrapper around the binary: configuration, routing, cooldowns, accounts/tokens, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible endpoints, CLI and every operation in `docs/integration/operations.md`. Add a parity manifest and checker on the meta-language model (`parity/…json` listing each feature with its JavaScript and Rust implementation and evidence), and shared fixtures/golden tests that both implementations must pass. Keep the existing wrapper package working, or merge it into the native package, without breaking downstream users.
3. **JavaScript first, Rust by translation.** New features and fixes land in JavaScript first, with tests. The Rust code is generated from the JavaScript source through meta-language translation, plus a regenerate-and-diff check, so generated Rust cannot drift. Where meta-language cannot translate a construct yet, report it to link-foundation/meta-language with a minimal example, and keep the hand-written Rust for that part small and listed in the parity manifest.
4. **Sub-agent workflow with a single push gate.** Document it in `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the agent instructions (`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`), and report what solve needs to support it to link-assistant/hive-mind:
   - **Drafting sub-agents** work in parallel on the full list of requirements and produce bulk drafts. They never push.
   - **One CI/CD sub-agent** is the only one allowed to push. It monitors the CI/CD runs of the branch, collects every failure of the latest run (all jobs, all logs), and has fixes drafted for all of them. It pushes **once**, when all of those fixes and the pending drafts are in, never fix by fix. It never pushes while a run is still in progress on the same commit range, so runs are not cancelled.
   - Before the push it runs the JavaScript checks locally (fast), and never full local Rust builds unless a Rust-only change requires it.
5. **Minimal local load.** Local and agent-container development runs JavaScript tests only by default. If Rust has to be built locally: one shared, bounded `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, reduced debug info, `-j` limited to the container's CPU/memory, and old artifacts pruned (`cargo-sweep` or equivalent). No per-work-dir 20–30 GiB `target/`.
6. **Rust CI/CD is gated on fully green JavaScript CI/CD.** It must be impossible to start any Rust job until the JavaScript stage has passed for the same commit:
   - One entry workflow whose Rust jobs `needs:` every JavaScript job (lint, tests, parity, translation regenerate-and-diff). Or separate Rust workflows triggered only by `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` of the JavaScript workflow and the same `head_sha`, with no `push`/`pull_request` triggers of their own.
   - A cancelled, skipped or partially successful JavaScript run must not start Rust. Path filters must not let a Rust-only change skip the JavaScript gate: the parity and translation checks always run.
   - Branch protection requires both stages. A per-branch `concurrency` group without cancel-in-progress for the Rust stage, so a gated Rust run is not thrown away by the next push.
   - A CI check that fails if any workflow can start Rust jobs without the JavaScript gate.
7. **Measure it.** Report before/after for a typical feature PR: pushes per PR, CI runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first fully green run, and peak local RSS/disk of an agent task.
8. **Apply it everywhere.** Write the approach as a reusable standard: the workflow gate (`needs:`/`workflow_run`), the parity manifest and checker, the translation regenerate-and-diff check, and the agent rules. Put it in the shared CI/CD templates (link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template and link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) and in link-assistant/hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Then open one issue per big Rust repository (at least link-assistant/formal-ai, link-foundation/meta-language, link-foundation/relative-meta-logic, link-foundation/link-cli, link-foundation/links-notation, link-foundation/start, link-assistant/calculator) to adopt it, each linking back here.
9. **Audit every mentioned repository and file issues for missing best practices.** For link-assistant/router itself and each repository in requirement 8, compare it against this standard, the two pipeline templates and `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`, and open an issue **in that repository** for every missing or broken best practice that no open issue already covers. Each issue needs evidence (files, workflows, run counts) and testable requirements, and links back here. The checklist:
   - native JavaScript implementation and a parity manifest plus checker run in CI for both languages;
   - Rust generated from JavaScript through meta-language, with a regenerate-and-diff check;
   - no Rust job can start before the JavaScript stage passes for the same commit, and no path filter bypasses the gate;
   - `concurrency` groups, and cancelled runs wasted by push-per-fix;
   - Rust build load: cargo profile/config, CI caching, pruning old artifacts;
   - agent instructions (`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`/`CONTRIBUTING.md`) for bulk drafting sub-agents with a single push gate;
   - differences from the templates (pinned actions, release/publish flow, link checks, security scans, false-positive/negative guards);
   - recurring failures on the default branch (for example a broken release job);
   - stale open pull requests.

Related: link-assistant/hive-mind#2889 (snapshot disk usage), link-assistant/hive-mind#2892 (OOM reporting), link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#36 (cargo-semver-checks cache).

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

issue.title: docker-snapshot resume copies the whole writable layer with no disk preflight, no serialization and no cleanup; offer a copy-free command resume

repository.name: start
repository.description: Gamification of coding, execute any command with ability to auto-report issues on GitHub

issue.body:
## Summary

`$ --resume <id> -- <command>` on a stopped Docker container (`docker-snapshot` mode) `docker commit`s the container's **whole writable layer** to `start-command-resume/<name>:<attempt>` and runs the command in a new `<name>-resume-<attempt>` container. Nothing bounds that copy:

1. **No free-disk preflight.** The commit starts even when the data root cannot hold it. On the containerd image store (the default for fresh Docker Engine 29 installs) a commit writes a compressed blob **and** an unpacked snapshot, while the original container stays on disk. Peak usage is about 3× the writable layer.
2. **No serialization.** `$ --resume` processes for different executions commit at the same time.
3. **No cleanup.** After the new container starts, the stopped original (all of its data is now in the image) is kept, and the `start-command-resume/*` image is never removed, even after the resumed container finishes and is removed.
4. **No copy-free way to run a different command in the same container.** `docker-start` mode (no command) re-runs the original `Config.Cmd`; anything else is a full commit. The `docker-cleanup.js` hint "Run another command in the same container: `$ --resume <id> -- <command>`" is misleading: it is a copy in a new container.

On containerd the commit is also slow regardless of the change size: the default differ (`doubleWalkDiff`) walks both full trees ([Sealos measured a 1 KB commit at 39 s and 10 GB at 847 s](https://sealos.io/blog/sealos-devbox-commit-performance-optimization/)).

## Incident

link-assistant/hive-mind#2889 (2026-10-09, start-command 0.35.4; the behaviour is unchanged in 0.36.0, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store). A dockerd restart killed four Rust build containers (writable layers 11, 21.2, 23.5 and 36.8 GiB, mostly Cargo `target/`). Their supervisor resumed all four with `$ --resume <uuid> -- <command>` within a minute. Four concurrent commits used about 280 % CPU for 30+ minutes and took free disk from 52 GB to 2 GB. Two commits failed with `failed to apply diff: … no space left on device`, and the two that succeeded left 11 + 23.5 GiB originals next to their images. (The record loss seen in the same incident was #193, fixed in #196.)

## Reproduction (bounded: 2 × 256 MiB, start-command 0.36.0)

```sh
for n in snap-a snap-b; do
  $ --isolated docker --detached --session $n --image alpine:3.20 -- sh -c 'dd if=/dev/zero of=/root/big bs=1M count=256; sleep 600'
done
sleep 6; docker kill snap-a snap-b

# The supervisor resumes both killed sessions with a command at the same time
$ --resume snap-a -- sh -c 'sleep 600' &
$ --resume snap-b -- sh -c 'sleep 600' &
wait

docker images 'start-command-resume/snap-*'     # a full copy of each layer
docker ps -a --filter name=snap-                # the stopped originals are still there
docker rm -f snap-a-resume-1 snap-b-resume-1    # the resumed containers are gone, the images stay:
docker images 'start-command-resume/snap-*'
```

Actual output (Docker 29.8.0, start-command 0.36.0; [script](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2889-b3cf2ad55a40/experiments/issue-2889-concurrent-snapshot-resume.sh), [log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2889-b3cf2ad55a40/docs/case-studies/issue-2889/data/concurrent-snapshot-resume-start-0.36.0.log)):

```
writable layers: /snap-a=268435456 /snap-b=268435456
snap-b: $ --resume ran from +0.95s to +6.55s
snap-a: $ --resume ran from +0.95s to +6.75s
docker events (seconds after both resumes started):
  +5.72s commit snap-b
  +6.16s commit snap-a
  +6.41s start snap-b-resume-1
  +6.62s start snap-a-resume-1
start-command-resume/snap-a:1 276MB
start-command-resume/snap-b:1 276MB
snap-a-resume-1 Up 2 seconds
snap-b-resume-1 Up 2 seconds
snap-b Exited (137) 13 seconds ago
snap-a Exited (137) 13 seconds ago
after the resumed containers are removed:
start-command-resume/snap-a:1 276MB
start-command-resume/snap-b:1 276MB
snap-b Exited (137) 15 seconds ago
snap-a Exited (137) 15 seconds ago
```

The two commits overlap completely. Nothing checked the free space first. Both originals and both images outlive the resumed containers. With the incident's layer sizes, the same sequence needs about 3 × 92.5 GiB at its peak.

(On 0.35.4 two concurrent resumes of the **same** execution both committed and the second failed only at `docker run` with a container-name conflict. The #196 launch reservation in 0.36.0 now rejects the second one: `Launch reservation failed: A different resume already reserved this execution`.)

A single resume behaves the same way (Docker 29.8.0, start-command 0.35.4, 64 MiB layer): `mode=docker-snapshot in 2511 ms; images: start-command-resume/<name>:2 74.9MB`, with the original container still present ([log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2889-b3cf2ad55a40/docs/case-studies/issue-2889/data/docker-start-handoff-experiment.log)).

## Workaround (used in hive-mind#2894)

Make the container itself accept a new command, so `docker start` (no copy) is enough. The container is created with a prefix:

```sh
h='/tmp/hive-mind-resume-command-<token>'; if [ -f "$h" ]; then exec sh "$h"; fi; <original command>
```

To run a new command in the stopped container, write it with `docker cp` (works on stopped containers), then `$ --resume <id>` **without** a command:

```sh
printf 'exec sh -c %s\n' "'echo recovered; ls /root'" > /tmp/cmd && docker cp /tmp/cmd snap-demo:/tmp/hive-mind-resume-command-<token>
$ --resume snap-demo        # mode docker-start: same container ID, same writable layer, nothing committed
```

Verified on Docker 29.8.0 with start-command 0.35.4 and 0.36.0: docker-start (643 ms on 0.35.4), the same container ID, the task's files present, and no image or `-resume-` container created. For containers that still need a snapshot, hive-mind now runs them one at a time and only with free space ≥ 2 × the writable layer + 10 GiB, and it removes the original with `docker rm` (not `-f`) after the new container starts. Images are removed with `docker rmi` when the task finishes.

## Suggested fix

1. **Copy-free command resume.** Offer a mode that runs a new command in the **same** container, e.g. `$ --resume <id> --in-place -- <command>`, or make it the default when the container was launched by start-command. Launch every detached docker container with a handoff prefix like the one above (start already uses the same `docker cp` marker technique for `--on-kill-resume` in `execution-recovery.js`). On resume, `docker cp` the command into the stopped container and `docker start` it. Fall back to `docker-snapshot` only for containers without the prefix.
2. **Preflight in `docker-snapshot`.** Before `docker commit`, read `docker inspect --size -f '{{.SizeRw}}'` and the free space of the data root (`docker info -f '{{.DockerRootDir}}'`, plus containerd's root when the containerd store is used). Refuse, or wait with a clear status, when free < 2 × SizeRw + a reserve. Report `snapshotting N GiB` in the status/log.
3. **Serialize snapshots** across `$` processes, for example with a host-wide lock file next to the execution store. Do not hold the store lock itself; see #193.
4. **Clean up.** Add an opt-in `--remove-original` (or a cleanup policy) to `docker rm` the stopped original once the snapshot container is running, and `docker rmi` the `start-command-resume/*` images when the resumed container is removed by the existing cleanup policy (`docker-cleanup.js`).
5. **Fix the hint** in `docker-cleanup.js`: "Run another command in the same container" should say that it snapshots the filesystem into a new container.

issue.title: feat(queue): keep the Telegram solve queue across bot and container restarts (#2890)

labels.name: formal-ai-draft
labels.description: Pull request drafted by the Formal AI draft workflow

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
Fixes #2890. On 2026-10-09 the host dockerd was OOM-killed, which killed the root `hive-mind` container. The 32 items in the Telegram solve queue (27 codex, 5 claude) were lost, because the queue existed only in the bot's memory. This PR keeps the queue in a links triple store on a host volume, with Telegram and the bot log as fallbacks. A restarted bot now continues the queue without manual action. The [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2890-553ce4602aa0/docs/case-studies/issue-2890/README.md) has the timeline, every requirement, root causes, research and evidence.

### What changes

**Every queue change is saved** (`src/telegram-solve-queue.persistence.lib.mjs`).
- `SolveQueue.notifyStateChange()` fires on enqueue, start, session assignment, card edit, finish, cancel and reject.
- Each save is a full snapshot, and saves are coalesced. A snapshot holds:
  - every queued, waiting and starting item, with its args, requester, chat, topic and command message, edited card, session id, status and timestamps;
  - the per-tool and global start times;
  - the statistics.
- Each change is also logged as a structured `EVENT queue_item_<event>` line.

**Triple store on the associative stack** (`src/solve-queue-store.lib.mjs`).
- Three copies are kept:
  - `solve-queue.links-archive`: a link-cli store archive (binary links notation, doublets and names);
  - `solve-queue.lino`: a readable Links Notation projection;
  - `solve-queue-db/solve-queue.links`: a clink database, rebuilt with `clink --import-binary --transactions` when `clink` is installed.
- The two files are written atomically: temp file, fsync, rename, then a directory fsync. They are mode 0600.
- Each copy carries a revision. On load the newest valid copy wins and the others are repaired.
- `links-notation` is pinned to 0.25.1 for `LinksPacket`.

**Restore on launch** (`src/telegram-solve-queue.durability.lib.mjs`, wired before `bot.launch()` in `src/telegram-bot.mjs`).
- Items go back in their original order. An interrupted start goes first, because the consumer always starts the head of a tool queue.
- A starting item whose session is still alive is handed to the session monitor, not run twice. This is checked against `sessions.json`, `$ --status` and active sessions for the URL.
- A start that never reached a container is queued again. After 3 interrupted starts the item is dropped, so a crashing task cannot loop forever; ordinary restarts never cost an item its place.
- Each chat and topic gets one notice in the item's locale ("Back in the queue: N, Still running: M").

**Fallbacks** (`src/telegram-solve-queue.telegram-backup.lib.mjs`, `src/telegram-solve-queue.log-recovery.lib.mjs`).
- The Bot API cannot read chat history. So with `HIVE_MIND_QUEUE_BACKUP_CHAT_ID` set, the bot keeps the `.lino` as a pinned document, at most once a minute, and reads it back from `getChat().pinned_message`.
- When there is no backup either, the queue is rebuilt from the bot logs in `HIVE_MIND_LOG_DIR` and from any file in `HIVE_MIND_QUEUE_RECOVERY_LOG`, such as a saved `docker logs`. Both the new `EVENT` lines and the incident's legacy `Enqueued:` and `Starting:` lines are read.

**Host volume and docs.**
- The store lives in `HIVE_MIND_STATE_DIR`, default `~/.hive-mind/state`.
- DOCKER, README, CONFIGURATION and COLLECTING-LOGS (en, ru, zh, hi) and `coolify/docker-compose.yml` mount `/root/.hive-mind/state` and `/root/.hive-mind/logs` to `/home/box/.hive-mind/…`.
- `helm/hive-mind/values.yaml` notes that the `/home/box` PVC already covers both.
- The Docker docs recommend `"live-restore": true` as a host mitigation.

**Verbose tracing.** `--verbose` prints `[VERBOSE] /queue-store:`, `/queue-backup:` and `/queue-restore:` lines. `EVENT queue_restored` records the source, revision and counts.

**Codebase-wide check.** The other queues, `hive.mjs`'s `IssueQueue` and `/merge`, are rebuilt from GitHub on every cycle, so they need no local state.

**Dependency freshness.** The PR's own run failed in `detect-changes` because Bun 1.4.3 was released while the PR was open. The three Dockerfiles now pin Bun 1.4.3. The Dockerfile installs Bun over the base image's copy, so `tests/test-issue-2187-runtime-versions.mjs` now pins Bun to the current release, the way it already pins Node.js, instead of to the version Box 2.10.3 ships.

### Reproduction and tests

| Test | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/test-issue-2890-solve-queue-store.mjs` | archive, `.lino` and clink round trips; stale, corrupt or missing stores repaired; atomic writes; byte-compatibility with `clink` |
| `tests/test-issue-2890-solve-queue-persistence.mjs` | item ↔ record ↔ link; coalesced saves; restore order (including equal timestamps), cards, timing and stats; reconciliation; restore limit |
| `tests/test-issue-2890-solve-queue-recovery.mjs` | bot launch restore, grouped notices, Telegram pinned backup, rebuild from the incident's log formats |
| `tests/test-issue-2890-solve-queue-kill.mjs` | `kill -9` of a child bot with queued, waiting, starting (alive and lost) items, a second tool, and a session in kill recovery. A new process restores and drains everything, each item exactly once and in order; a later restart restores nothing; 3 more rounds kill during saves and check that the stored queue is a consistent prefix |
| `experiments/issue-2890-docker-kill.mjs` | `docker kill` (137) + `docker rm` of a real container with the state dir mounted. Log: `docs/case-studies/issue-2890/evidence/docker-kill-experiment.log` |
| `examples/solve-queue-restart-demo.mjs` | the stored `.lino` and the chat notice after a restart |

Before this change, the restarted bot showed `Completed: 0, Failed: 0` and every queue at `pending: 0`. After it, the queue comes back as the tests above show. Writing the demo found a bug: items queued in the same millisecond put the interrupted start last. It is fixed, and the persistence test covers it.

### Upstream

- [link-foundation/link-cli#112](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/issues/112): `clink --out` writes numeric names like addresses, so its LiNo export does not round-trip through `--import`. It has a repro (`experiments/issue-2890-clink-numeric-names.mjs`), a workaround and a suggested fix. Hive Mind is not affected: it syncs clink through the binary archive only.
- [link-foundation/disk-space-saviour#22](https://github.com/link-foundation/disk-space-saviour/issues/22): the `docker diff` storm that OOM-killed dockerd. Already reported and closed.

### Limitations

- Commands sent while the bot is down are still dropped (`dropPendingUpdates`).
- Tasks inside the root container die with it. They are left to kill recovery (#2887–#2889), whose counters now live on the same volume.
- Without the `state` mount, `docker rm` still loses the store. The log fallback then needs the old `docker logs` saved.
- The incident notes do not say why `--restart unless-stopped` did not restart the root container on 2026-10-09.
